mayor's Youth Council and state of the youth address jam spires office of youth alternatives and staff advisor to the mayor's Youth Council president Rini members of the governing body parents and members of the public where are you tonight on a special occasion to recognize and celebrate the 2017-2018 class of the mayor's Youth Council we also will commemorate their service to the community and what they have learned by serving on the Youth Council this year we will start with a state of the u.s. address it will be given by Julia Horst this year's chair Julia is a junior at Central High and she will share some of the group's projects and what they have learned during their time this year on the Youth Council Julia Context/Agenda: president Rini and members of mayor's Youth Council of City Council I am doing a horse and I am here Context/Agenda: I am here to represent the mayor's Youth Council tonight I have been on the mayor's Youth Council for three years and I think this year may have been my favorite we have accomplished many wonderful things this year including numerous volunteer projects to benefit our community in December we put on our annual cookie decorating extravaganza in conjunction with the special friends program at youth alternatives we invited children from Cheyenne to join us at the Children's Village for a couple hours of holiday fun recently we also got involved with the VA here in Cheyenne we decided to focus our projects around the VA because we felt the veterans in Cheyenne often go unnoticed and we recognized profound impact a group of interested teenagers could have on veterans who don't often get much time with youth after taking a tour of the VA we sat down with some of the veterans and talked about research we had done on the USS Lexington as well as listen to their stories and shared some stories of our own we also volunteered to clean up the courtyard at the VA by clearing out weeds and dead plants in the garden areas so that new plants could grow and the veterans could come and enjoy the nice weather through our involvement at the VA I think as a group we learned a lot about the lives of veterans and the value of face-to-face conversations with them in addition to the various projects we did we also had many opportunities to learn about the city of Cheyenne we learned about the basics of city government certainly that bites into family time so thank you Mary Ann for lending us your husband for the past year for his service as president and at this time I'd like to present you with a plaque and then
